title: Elements, compounds & formulae
examples: How do I know if something is an element or a compound?
If I see the formula H2O, what does that tell me?
Can you show me how to write the formula for magnesium oxide?

explain.say: Today we will learn about chemical symbols and formulas. You will learn to count atoms in compounds.
Each element has a unique symbol. For example, oxygen is always represented by the letter O.
When we write a formula, the numbers tell us how many atoms are present. For water, H2O, there are two hydrogen atoms.
To write a formula, we combine the symbols using the correct ratios. For carbon dioxide, we use the symbols C and O2.
In the compound magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2, we count atoms in groups. There are one magnesium atom and two hydroxide groups.
In everyday life, you see formulas on medicine bottles. They tell you the exact chemical makeup of the drug.

faq.q: What is the difference between an element and a compound?
faq.a: An element is a pure substance made of only one type of atom, like gold. A compound is made when two or more different elements chemically combine, like water.

faq.q: How do I know how many atoms are in a formula like Al2(SO4)3?
faq.a: You count the subscript numbers. The number outside the parenthesis multiplies everything inside, and then you add up all the atoms.
asks: How do I count atoms in complex formulas?
What does the big number outside the brackets mean?

faq.q: Do I need to memorize every element symbol?
faq.a: You need to know the symbols for the elements you are studying right now. Some common ones are very important to remember.
asks: Which symbols are the most important?
Is there a chart for symbols?

faq.q: Why do we use parentheses in chemical formulas?
faq.a: Parentheses group atoms together so you know which atoms are counted by the number outside the group. This keeps the count correct.
asks: What is the purpose of the brackets?
When do I use parentheses in formulas?

faq.q: If I see a formula like N2O4, does that mean two nitrogen and four oxygen atoms?
faq.a: Yes, that is correct. The subscript number directly tells you the number of atoms for that element in the formula.
asks: Does the number after the symbol mean atoms?
Is N2O4 two N and four O?

facts: Elements are the simplest pure substances that cannot be broken down further.
Chemical formulas use symbols to represent elements combined in a specific ratio.
Subscripts indicate the number of atoms of an element in a compound.
Parentheses are used to group polyatomic ions when counting atoms.

quiz.say: What is the chemical symbol for Sodium?
quiz.why: Sodium is an element, and its symbol is Na, which comes from its Latin name.

wrong.1: This is the symbol for Sulfur, which is a different element.
wrong.2: Symbols are usually one or two letters, not two separate letters like this.
wrong.3: This shows a charge, which is not just the element symbol.

quiz.say: How many oxygen atoms are in the formula Ca(OH)2?
quiz.why: The subscript two outside the parenthesis applies to everything inside, so there are two oxygen atoms.

wrong.0: You are only counting the oxygen atoms, not the total atoms in the compound.
wrong.1: This answers the number of hydrogen atoms, not the oxygen atoms.
wrong.3: You must remember that the subscript two applies to the oxygen inside the group.

quiz.say: A compound has 2 atoms of Nitrogen and 1 atom of Oxygen. What is its formula?
quiz.why: Two nitrogen atoms means N2, and one oxygen atom means O, so the formula is N2O.

wrong.1: This would mean one nitrogen and two oxygen atoms.
wrong.2: This would mean two nitrogen and two oxygen atoms.
wrong.3: Parentheses are only needed if the group repeats, like in Ca(OH)2.
